metadata.title: H-E-B, Southwest, Dell lead Forbes' best Texas companies list

content.text:
Texas grocery giant H-E-B tops Forbes' new list of the state's best companies, and Tesla comes in last.
On Nov. 12, Forbes announced its second annual America's Best Companies Best-in-State list, which identifies less-prominent companies whose performance stands out.
The list highlights small companies in smaller states that are often overlooked in Forbes' annual America's Best Companies list, which is dominated by sizable companies based in states like California, New York and Texas.
Forbes analyzed about 5,000 companies nationwide, the largest employers in each state. Each state, depending on its population, received approximately five to 25 listees. A total of 750 made the final list.
Texas' list included notable companies like Tesla, Southwest Airlines, and Oracle, as well as Texas staples like Dell, H-E-B, and Dr. Pepper. The list also includes lesser-known real estate and energy companies.
Forbes' Texas Best-in-State companies
Here's who made Texas' list and where they are located in the state:
-
H-E-B Grocery Company (San Antonio)
-
Southwest Airlines (Dallas)
-
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (Spring)
-
Dell Technologies (Round Rock)
-
Baker Hughes Company (Houston)
-
Quanta Services (Houston)
-
Waste Management (Houston)
-
ExxonMobil (Spring)
-
TaskUs (New Braunfels)
-
Essilor of America (Dallas)
-
AECOM (Dallas)
-
Ryan (Dallas)
-
Toyota North America (Plano)
-
Jacobs Solutions (Dallas)
-
ENGIE North America (Houston)
-
Oracle (Austin)
-
Sysco (Houston)
-
Risepoint (Dallas)
-
Fluor (Irving)
-
Keurig Dr Pepper (Frisco)
-
Weatherford International (Houston)
-

-
CBRE Group (Dallas)
-
Energy Transfer (Dallas)
-
Tesla (Austin)
